old_article_2.title: 10 Ways to Plan a Magical Candlelit Wedding Reception
h2s: Here are 10 ways to plan a dreamy candlelit wedding reception:
1 . Work with an event designer who understands your vision.
2. Take the weather and time of day into account.
3. Enhance the design with fairy lights.
9. Dark color scheme around it for contrast
10. Create a fairytale setting with abundant florals.
old_article_2.note: Item 1 text is truncated on the live page (starts mid-sentence 'right on track.'). Links out to designers' Instagram accounts (Alice Wilkes, Julia & Evita, Cerka Creative, With Love Inc.); all images are credited to those accounts, not ours to reuse. US spelling ('color', 'cozy'). Cannibalisation: partial overlap with candle section; decide 301 or keep as a candle-specific support page linked from the new guide.

old_article_claims.claim: A wedding designer is equipped with all the technical expertise needed to execute a candlelit wedding reception that ... is completely safe.
old_article_claims.note: Safety guarantee with no source. Replace with venue rules in writing plus official fire service rules (F-10, F-14, F-15).

old_article_claims.claim: Your event designer can work with your wedding planner to comply with the safety regulations of the venue, study whether the rain or wind on the day will affect the setup.
old_article_claims.note: Consistent with F-06 and F-09.

old_article_claims.claim: Outdoor weddings typically see candles encased in glass jars, which seal them off from wind.
old_article_claims.note: Keep as hurricane glass advice (F-03, F-09). Glass does not exempt a flame from a Total Fire Ban: not stated as exempt by NSW RFS, CFA or QFD.

old_article_claims.claim: Fairy lights ... don't wash out the candlelit feel, yet provide enough additional brightness.
old_article_claims.note: Add outdoor-rated, IP23+, extra-low-voltage advice (F-20).

old_article_claims.claim: Floating candles: suspending candles from an overhead bar or cable using thin wires.
old_article_claims.note: Suspended open flame. Many venues ban naked flame (F-07); recommend LED or flameless for suspended pieces and confirm rigging (F-06). Not a sky lantern, which is a separate banned product (F-17).

old_article_claims.claim: Group candles of various height and width together.
old_article_claims.note: Matches F-03.

old_article_claims.claim: If your photographer will be using a drone, set up an entire garden of candles ... hundreds of tea lights.
old_article_claims.note: Hundreds of open flames on the ground outdoors conflicts with fire ban rules on TFB days and with venue rules. Reframe as LED tea lights or check venue and fire danger rating. Drone rules not researched (CASA), leave out or add to gaps.

old_article_claims.claim: Place candles on a mirrored surface to magnify their light ... won't require a tablecloth.
Candles and glass cylinders of congruent height in a straightforward line.
Use dark colors in your background ... elaborate candelabras as key centerpieces.
old_article_claims.note: Matches F-05 (dark perimeter).

old_article_claims.claim: Soft candlelight and decadent, overgrown blooms ... you'll feel just like a princess.
old_article_claims.note: Tone is off-brand; drop 'princess'. Keep flames clear of foliage: style advice only, no official source on clearance for candles (CFA 3 m rule applies to fire pits, F-16).

old_article_2.verdict: Better than the 2017 post but generic, truncated item 1, unsourced safety guarantee, and two ideas (suspended candles, hundreds of ground tea lights) now need safety framing. Keep items 2, 5, 7, 8, 9 as ideas; rewrite 1, 4, 6.

facts.claim: Plan the light from daylight to dark. The room has to look finished before the candles read. Light the focal point first, then the tables, and keep every source warm white.
facts.use_note: Own page; link as related Style Advice. Keep wording consistent.

facts.claim: Spend on light. It decides how every surface reads after dusk and is the hardest thing to fix on the day. On a terrace that means festoon over the tables and warm uplight on the stone, and in a ballroom a pin spot on each centrepiece.
facts.use_note: Own page; overlap risk, so expand rather than repeat.

facts.claim: Group tapers of two or three heights in clusters about an arm's length apart, rather than spacing single candles evenly. Where the villa allows flame in glass only, use hurricane glass, and where it allows none, put battery candles in the same holders.
facts.use_note: Villa section; own wording.

facts.claim: In an olive grove, keep every flame in glass and off dry grass, light the trees from below with warm uplights, and string festoon lights over the long table ... line the paths with lanterns.
facts.use_note: Vineyard and grove guidance.

facts.claim: If the room is already gilded, don't match it with gold: dim the house lights, keep the perimeter dark, and put white light on the stage and tables so gold and ivory both read. If your room doesn't divide ... leave anything outside those zones unlit.
facts.use_note: Ballroom guidance. Note: this says 'white light' for gilded rooms while F-01 says 'warm white'; writer should say warm white generally and white on focal point in a gilded room.

facts.claim: Ask the hotel in writing for rigging points and the weight each holds, fabric fire ratings, load-in hours, and whether an outside decorator pays a fee or works beside the in-house team.
facts.use_note: Use for chandelier and installation section.

facts.claim: Hall Place, a Grade I listed Tudor house in Bexley, does not permit confetti, rose petals, naked flames, smoke or haze machines, and its ceremony hire includes LED candles.
facts.use_note: Venue example of a no-naked-flame rule. Primary source is https://www.hallplace.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Hall-Place-The-Ceremony-Experience-26-27-28.pdf (not re-read in fast mode). Use only as 'some historic venues ban naked flame'.

facts.claim: On a long, light summer evening the candles won't read until late, so light the marquee before you dress it and make sure it looks finished in daylight.
facts.use_note: Marquee and summer timing.

facts.claim: A headland is harder than a beach, because the wind comes side-on and rarely drops ... put candles in tall hurricane glass. During a NSW total fire ban you can't light or use a fire in the open, so have battery candles ready for the same holders.
facts.use_note: Own wording; the fire ban rule itself must be cited to NSW RFS (see official facts).

facts.claim: A total fire ban means no fires out in the open. During a Total Fire Ban you cannot light, maintain or use a fire in the open, or to carry out any activity in the open that causes, or is likely to cause, a fire.
facts.use_note: Core rule for outdoor candles, lanterns and fire pits in NSW. Page does not name candles specifically; writer must say 'fire in the open', not 'candles are banned'. Page modified 2026-11-10.

facts.claim: A barbeque or wood fire pizza oven which uses solid fuel, such as wood, charcoal or heat beads, cannot be used outside during a Total Fire Ban. Permits are suspended on days of total fire ban.
facts.use_note: Relevant if a wood-fired feature or pizza oven doubles as lighting or catering.

facts.claim: A range of activities may be exempt from Total Fire Bans, such as ... use of fireworks or ceremonial fires. The RFS Commissioner is responsible for exemptions ... detailed in the NSW Government Gazette each time a Total Fire Ban is declared ... a minimum of 21 days processing time is required for us to assess your application.
facts.use_note: Exemptions are conditional and gazetted per ban; do not imply weddings are exempt. Use '21 days' only to say a specific exemption cannot be arranged at short notice.

facts.claim: Lighting a fire on a day of Total Fire Ban attracts an on the spot fine of $2200. If the matter goes to court, you could be subject to a fine of up to $5500 and/or 12 months gaol.
facts.use_note: Penalty, not a price. Optional; brief says avoid scare tactics, so use sparingly if at all.

facts.claim: 'Open air' means any place that is not inside a permanent structure with a roof and fully enclosed walls. Caravans are considered permanent structures, but tents are not.
facts.use_note: Key for marquees: in Victoria a tent counts as open air, so a marquee does not take open flame outside TFB rules. Page last updated 10 Nov 2026 (Victorian caretaker period notice shown).

facts.claim: All fires for warmth or personal comfort including fire pits, braziers and chimineas are banned during Total Fire Ban Days.
facts.use_note: Fire pit lounges at vineyard receptions. CFA page does not mention candles specifically; do not claim it does.

facts.claim: During the Fire Danger Period a fire for warmth or comfort in a fire pit, brazier or chiminea is not allowed unless the wind is not more than 10km/h, it is lit in a properly-constructed fireplace, the area within 3 metres is clear of flammable material, the fire does not exceed 1 square metre, and a person is in attendance at all times with the capacity and means to extinguish it.
facts.use_note: Paraphrased condition list from the FDP tab; writer may summarise as 'conditions on wind, clearance and a person in attendance'.

facts.claim: There is a permanent ban on sky lanterns because they are a fire and burn risk ... If a product is banned, it must not be supplied in Australia. Sky lanterns can also be called floating lanterns or flying lanterns.
facts.use_note: Ban is on supply (Consumer Protection Notice No. 17 of 2011). Writer should say 'banned from supply in Australia', not 'illegal to release', unless a state source is added. Replaces the old page's 'floating lanterns' idea. accc.gov.au is approved; productsafety.gov.au added to domains.md.

facts.claim: To purchase, use, store, manufacture, supply and transport fireworks you need a licence. ... [licence holders must] only use the fireworks for an organised public event and have a supporting letter from the local Council stating they have no objections.
facts.use_note: NSW only. Fireworks at a reception need a licensed pyrotechnician arranged through the venue. Page does not mention sparklers; see gaps.

facts.claim: Portable generators should never be used indoors or in enclosed areas. They emit carbon monoxide that you cannot see or smell, and may cause carbon monoxide poisoning and asphyxiation very quickly, and death. ... Only use heavy-duty extension cords that are in good condition and rated in watts or amps at least equal to the rating of the generator. Protect connection points between extension cords and appliances from the weather.
facts.use_note: Page is written for households in power outages, not events. Use as general principle: generator outside, away from marquees and guests, run by the hire company or a licensed electrician. Reviewed 16 March 2026. ESV search summary mentioned 'tents' but the page itself says 'indoors or in enclosed areas'; quote the page.

facts.claim: Outdoor Christmas lights have an IP rating number (e.g. IPX3, IP23, IP44) showing how weatherproof the light is: outdoor equipment must have a rating of at least IP23. ... Only use lights intended for outdoors: all outdoor connections and lights must be weatherproof. Use solar powered lights, LED or extra-low-voltage lights (5V, 12V or 24V): these are the safest options to prevent electric shock and fires caused by over-heating.
facts.use_note: Christmas and decorative lighting page; applies by analogy to festoon and fairy lights. Say 'Energy Safe Victoria's guidance on decorative lights'. Reviewed 27 Aug 2024. Original uses en dashes; reworded with colons here to keep no-dash rule.

facts.claim: Don't run electrical leads over walkways or driveways where they may be damaged. ... Secure outdoor lights and decorations to avoid damage in wind or storms and turn them off in poor weather. ... Flood lights, halogen lights and other high powered lights can become very hot: keep them away from anything that might catch fire.
facts.use_note: Cables across a lawn aisle or dance floor; uplights near drape.

facts.claim: Test your safety switch ... if you don't have safety switch, get one installed or use a portable safety switch. Use power boards fitted with over-load protection: avoid using double adaptors or piggy backing plugs.
facts.use_note: Private villa or estate weddings using house power.

facts.claim: The use of open flame fire pits, braziers, and similar devices is not permitted during a fire ban. Open flames and embers present a high fire risk under these conditions.
facts.use_note: Queensland uses declared local fire bans, not the NSW or Victorian Total Fire Ban term. Page last updated 31 July 2026. Candles not named.

facts.claim: Private use of fireworks is illegal in Queensland. However, fireworks can be used for official events during a fire ban period as long as the licenced firework contractors have notified Queensland Fire Department and Resources Safety and Health Queensland (RSHQ).
facts.use_note: Source sentence is garbled ('if fireworks can be used'); quoted as cleaned. Licensed contractor only.

facts.claim: All permits to light fires are automatically cancelled during a fire ban ... Fire Wardens cannot override a fire ban.
facts.use_note: Supports 'a permit arranged weeks earlier can still fall on a ban day, so keep flameless backups'.

facts.claim: Gas (butane or propane) and electric barbecues, including gas and spirit stoves, can be used during fire bans, as long as they do not have the potential to make embers or ignite nearby ground fuels and vegetation, are not left unattended, are suitably contained.
facts.use_note: Cooking, not lighting. Do not extend to gas-fuelled decorative flame features or gas lanterns: not stated. Conflicts with CFA, which bans liquid fuels such as methylated spirits outdoors on TFB days; state rules differ, so cite by state.

facts.claim: Is open flame allowed, allowed only when enclosed, or not allowed at all? Are tapers allowed, or only pillars in glass? Can anything be fixed to beams, walls, the ceiling or marquee poles? ... Some hotels and country houses ban naked flame outright, so get every answer in writing before you brief the florist.
facts.use_note: Own venue question list; link rather than repeat.

facts.claim: Where flame must be enclosed, tall hurricane glass or flameless pillars at two or three heights keep the gold catching light.
facts.use_note: Ballroom candle advice.

facts.claim: Keep table candles unscented, and view a lit sample table after dark before you sign off, because tonal linen and matte ceramics can read flat under evening light. Use stable, non-combustible holders and name one person with a snuffer.
facts.use_note: This page links to both incumbent posts as 'planning a candlelit reception' and 'using lighting across the day'; update those links if they are 301'd.

facts.claim: On a Total Fire Ban day you cannot light a fire in the open, so ask your venue in writing whether that covers table candles.
facts.use_note: House framing for the candle question; consistent with F-10. Keep the same 'ask your venue in writing' wording.

facts.claim: Dubai Civil Defence's published rules don't address table candles, so plan on enclosed or flameless ones until your hotel confirms.
facts.use_note: Own earlier finding, not re-verified against Dubai Civil Defence in this run. Usable for a UAE ballroom line; otherwise treat as a gap.

facts.claim: Wax on hire: Ask how your hire firm charges for wax on linen and glass, and use dripless tapers. Draughts on flame: Weight the linen and put every flame in glass where air moves.
facts.use_note: Day-of risks.

legal.summary: During a Total Fire Ban no fire may be lit, maintained or used in the open; permits are suspended; exemptions (including fireworks and ceremonial fires) are gazetted per ban by the RFS Commissioner. Confirmed by NSW Rural Fire Service.
Open air is anywhere not inside a permanent structure with a roof and fully enclosed walls; tents are open air. Fire pits, braziers and chimineas banned on TFB days. Confirmed by CFA.
Permanent ban on supply of sky lanterns (also called floating or flying lanterns), Consumer Protection Notice No. 17 of 2011. Confirmed by ACCC Product Safety.
A licence is needed to purchase, use or store fireworks; displays only for organised events with council support. Confirmed by SafeWork NSW.
Open flame fire pits and braziers not permitted during a declared fire ban; permits cancelled; private fireworks illegal, licensed contractors only. Confirmed by Queensland Fire Department.

gaps.handling: Write 'fire in the open' and 'ask your venue in writing whether that covers candles' (F-30). Never state candles are banned or allowed.

gaps.handling: Do not recommend sparklers as DIY. Say fireworks need a licensed operator (F-18, F-24) and ask the venue.

gaps.what: State-level rule on releasing sky lanterns (as opposed to the national supply ban).
gaps.handling: Say 'banned from supply in Australia' only (F-17).

gaps.what: Event-specific electrical rules for temporary lighting (testing and tagging, licensed electrician for marquee power). ESV pages found are household guidance only; NSW Fair Trading and Qld Electrical Safety Office not checked in fast mode.
gaps.handling: Cite ESV as guidance on decorative lights (F-20 to F-22) and generators (F-19); otherwise 'ask your lighting supplier or venue electrician'.

gaps.what: Destination rules on candles, fireworks or sky lanterns (Bali, Italy, Greece, Fiji, UAE). Not researched in fast mode; Dubai only via our own page (F-31).
gaps.handling: Use 'check with your venue' for every destination.

gaps.what: WA, SA, Tasmania, ACT and NT fire ban rules not checked.
gaps.handling: Cite NSW, Vic and Qld by state only; do not generalise to 'Australia'.

gaps.what: Drone use over a candle garden (old_article_2 item 6). CASA rules not researched.
Hall Place primary PDF not re-read (F-07).
gaps.handling: Use only as 'some historic venues ban naked flame'.
